podcast.title: Absence During Brian Epstein Rehearsal
podcast.body: Mickey Willett was on holiday in Manchester during the week that Brian Epstein came to see The Bull Weevils rehearse, leaving the group "drummerless" for this critical audition. "Mickey Willett had gone on holiday to Manchester that week, and the group were drummerless."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 119: "You Really Got Me" by the Kinks

podcast.title: Conflict and Departure
podcast.body: Mickey Willett became suspicious about the band's finances and took on the role of the group's "self-appointed shop steward," frequently clashing with managers Robert Wace and Grenville Collins. Due to these "constant rouse with their management," Willett was "edged out of the group" by Wace and Collins, leading to The Ravens continuing with a temporary drummer. "Mickey Willett started to get suspicious about what was happening to all of the money, and became essentially the group's self-appointed shop steward, getting into constant rouse with their management."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 119: "You Really Got Me" by the Kinks

podcast.title: Connection to Robert Wace & Grenville Collins
podcast.body: Mickey Willett, an "experienced musician" with industry contacts, was instrumental in connecting The Bull Weevils with Robert Wace and Grenville Collins. A friend of Willett's in the music business pointed Wace and Collins, who were looking for a backing band for Wace, in the direction of The Bull Weevils. "Willett was an experienced musician who had contacts in the business, and so when I reached Deletante wannabe pop star named Robert Ways, and his best friend and manager Grembal Collins were looking for a backing band for Ways."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
